findings.summary: The terminal-state reader looks for `termination` as a TOP-LEVEL key of each journal.jsonl line, but a real journal line is a JournalEntry whose node stdout is nested as an escaped STRING in `result` — so the entry can never exit 0 and criterion 8 / Z1 is unreachable by construction. loop-engine writes exactly one journal line per node via `appendJournal(e)` = `JSON.stringify(entry)` (src/sink-file.ts:134-136), where `entry = { ...base, result: env.result, effects: env.effects }` and `base = { run_id, identity, spawned_by }` (src/engine.ts:1259,1289; single write point at src/engine.ts:895-898). For the tick bash node, `parseEnvelope(stdout)` throws because `tick-entry --run` prints `JSON.stringify(outcome, null, 2)` (src/tick-entry.ts:167) and `RunWriteOutcome` has NO `result` key (channelId/messageCount/decisions/writes/skipped/spawns/harvestReports/triageReports/hasPendingWork/termination, src/tick-run.ts:1021-1043) while `Envelope` requires `result: z.string()` (loop-engine src/types.ts:49-55); so the bash adapter falls back to `envelope = { result: r.stdout.trim(), effects: [] }` (loop-engine src/adapters/bash.ts:100-107). The real line is therefore `{"run_id":"tick~1","identity":"tick","result":"{\n  \"channelId\": …, \"termination\": {…}\n}","effects":[]}` — loop-engine's own assertions confirm `result` is a string carrying stdout (test/live/workflow-bash-loop.test.ts:61-62, workflow-bash-timeout.test.ts:118-119) and docs/spec.md:53 documents the line as `{run_id, identity, result, effects, spawned_by}`. Consequently `obj.termination && typeof obj.termination === "object"` is never true, `lastTermination` stays null, the script exits 1, e0-verify sets FAIL TERMINAL (bin/e0-verify.sh:69-71) and bin/e0-regression.sh returns 3 on a fully healthy run that reached a real terminal state. This is the same 'entry can never reach a passing Z1' shape that already rejected E0a and attempts 1-3, now one layer deeper: the sibling extractor that DOES work in production, scripts/check-drain-failures.mjs:73, deliberately substring-matches the whole line (`line.match(/\[bash 非零退出 EXIT:(\d+)\]/)`) precisely because the payload lives inside the escaped `result` string, not at the top level.

The discriminating coverage for the terminal assertion is built on a fabricated journal.jsonl contract that no producer emits, which is exactly the fixture-vs-reality shape spec §1.3 / §4 forbid and the reason this package exists. `makeEngineRoot` writes the bare tick run_output object as the journal line (`writeFileSync(join(runDir, "journal.jsonl"), `${runOutput}\n`)` where runOutput = `{channelId, …, termination:{state,…}}`), and T-VERIFY-DRAIN repeats the same fabrication at test/e0-regression.test.ts:759-779. Real journal lines are JournalEntry wrappers with stdout nested as a string in `result` — and this very repo already encodes the correct shape in its own fixture for the sibling extractor: test/g15-drain-failure-visible.test.ts:122-131 writes `JSON.stringify({ run_id: "tick~1", identity: "tick", result })`. Two contradictory journal fixtures now coexist in one test suite and the E0 one is the wrong one, so the suite goes green against a fictional bus/journal contract while the production path is broken (finding 1). T-VERIFY-DRAIN does not rescue this: its fake `dist/cli.js` only echoes a drain summary and never writes journal.jsonl, so the 'real driver' argument covers only the drain-summary hop while the journal hop remains hand-authored in the shape the engine never produces. Mutating scripts/e0-terminal-state.mjs to read the REAL shape would turn these tests red, which is the inverse of the discriminative requirement in §1.3 / criterion 3.

Non-blocking: the head_seq and sum work required by §1.1 / §1.2 is done correctly and is discriminative. scripts/e0-metrics.mjs reads only the list endpoint GET /v1/channels, looks up by channel_id, keeps each entry's actual field set for the loud failure, refuses to treat a read-miss as 0, and sums over all channels via real JSON.parse; test/e0-metrics.test.ts:18-34 pins the true full sum (18887 / 60) so the E0a greedy-sed implementation would go red, and test/fixtures/fake-bus.mjs:97-111 now matches the real contract (single-channel GET omits head_seq, list GET carries it) with T-FIXTURE-CONTRACT asserting both directions. Both original E0a blockers are genuinely fixed; only the terminal-state evidence path above blocks this package.
